perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to the following:

- He is a Project Manager. He feels frustrated and anxious because his project is falling behind and he believes his team is unmotivated.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and friend/trusted advisor, and he chooses to meet Arthur at a coffee shop for advice.
- In the coffee-shop conversation, Harold tells Arthur that his team seems unmotivated and that it is affecting progress. He hears Arthur:
  - acknowledge that motivation is tricky,
  - ask whether Harold has tried to understand what drives each team member individually,
  - suggest one-on-one conversations to learn personal motivations,
  - explain that people need to feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold decides to try Arthur’s suggestion and feels more hopeful.
- Harold then tells his team he wants to try quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He says he will schedule time with each of them and asks them to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold observes that the team is still not responding well to the new strategies. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold tells Arthur that he tried the suggestions but the team still is not responding well. He hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold decides to set up another round of meetings.
- In those one-on-one meetings, Harold asks team members to share concerns or problems. He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension between a few people affecting their work. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by the workload and find it hard to stay motivated when stressed. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and redistributing tasks, and tells them their well-being is important.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He believes addressing individual concerns will improve team performance. He tells the team he will implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment. He hears Team Member 1 and Team Member 2 respond positively. He says their input and well-being are crucial to the project’s success.

He does not have access to any private thoughts, hidden motivations, or unspoken information from Arthur or the team members unless they told him directly.
